target_roles._comment: Explicit titles Lucy is looking for. The AI scorer treats 'must_match_one' as a strong positive signal but doesn't require exact wording.
target_roles._fuzzy_comment: Broader categories the AI considers as positive matches if the title fits the spirit, even with different wording.
fuzzy_categories: any insurance graduate scheme open to school leavers
any junior risk or underwriting support role

role_relevance._comment: Title-only pre-filter that runs BEFORE hard_exclusions. Any title containing one of these substrings is dropped silently (does not appear in 'Set aside'). Use this for roles that are clearly off-topic regardless of seniority - software engineers, designers, lawyers, etc. Keep this list narrow: if a target role might use a word, leave it out. Match is case-insensitive substring on title only.

hard_exclusions._comment: If a posting's text matches any of these patterns it is filtered out before the AI scorer ever sees it. Saves Anthropic API tokens and avoids wasting Lucy's attention.
hard_exclusions._experience_comment: Patterns are matched against title + description with re.IGNORECASE. Use \b word boundaries for short common words to avoid false positives ('lead' must not match 'leading' or 'leader' in any sentence describing the team).

lookback._comment: First run goes wide so Lucy gets a snapshot of the live market. After that we narrow to ~last day with a small buffer in case a cron fires late. The seen_jobs dedup is the real safety net against duplicates - this filter is purely about scope.
